ana: Quick bring-up note: quill-embed-small-v2 showed a non-uniform quality regression after INT4 per-channel quant. Overall recall@1 on BEIR subset dropped noticeably, but the effect is concentrated in a handful of topical cohorts (legal, aviation). Posting numbers and what I ran.

ana: Numbers (BEIR-50 subset, same harness):
- fp16 recall@1: 0.642
- int8 (symmetric) recall@1: 0.639 (-0.5)
- int4 per-channel recall@1: 0.611 (-4.9)
- fp16 recall@20: 0.883
- int4 recall@20: 0.860 (-2.6)
Cluster purity (kmeans=150) fp16: 0.51 -> int4: 0.45.

drew: Oof. Can you share the eval command, whitening/normalization, and the exact quant pipeline? Did you fold norms and any fused ops?

ana: Sure, command I used:```bash
python eval/embeddings_eval.py --model quill-embed-small-v2 --weights /models/quill/v2/int4_pc.pt \ 
  --holdout s3://redwood-evals/beir_subset/50.jsonl --k 1 --batch 256 --sim dot --normalize false --whiten none
```
Quant pipeline (offline):```bash
python quant/quantize.py --checkpoint /checkpoints/quill/v2/fp16.ckpt --bits 4 --scheme per-channel --method mse-min --fold-layernorm true --block-size 1 --calib s3://redwood-evals/anchors/10k.jsonl
```
I left normalize=false to check raw dot; earlier teams normalize then whiten in downstream.

claire: Two quick thoughts: 1) If normalization was off, quant can change vector norms and dot will blow up; cosine vs dot will behave differently. 2) The topical concentration suggests per-dim bias shift (some dims encode niche jargon). Did you check per-dim mean shifts between fp16 and int4 on the 10k anchor set?

ana: I computed per-dim delta-mean and delta-std across anchors. A handful of dims had mean shifts >0.12 and std compressions ~20%. Also UMAP of cluster 'aviation' shows centroid moved ~0.18 cosine distance from fp16.

claire: Let's try a small calibration suite: A) per-dim affine correction (learn offset + scale on anchors), B) isotonic recalibration of similarity scores (learned monotonic map), C) normalization-then-whiten pipeline (length-norm -> PCA128 -> length-norm) to see if canonicalization helps. Also test dot vs cosine.

drew: Add a targeted cohort test (legal, aviation, single-token queries) and a stability stress: random swap neighbor test where we perturb each query embedding by Gaussian sigma=0.015 and measure top-5 swap rate. If int4 increases swap rate non-linearly, it's a fail for production.

ana: Queued experiments: run_id=1789999999-a (affine-calib), run_id=1789999999-b (isotonic-sim-calib), run_id=1789999999-c (norm+PCA128). Configs: s3://redwood-dev/quill/onboard/1789999999/*.yaml. Anchors used: s3://redwood-evals/anchors/10k.jsonl.

marta-bot: Note: please include memory/perf footprint for mixed-precision options. INT4 perf gains may be marginal if we add expensive online calibration.

ana: Good call — will record latency and p99 token costs for each profile. Also adding a hybrid profile (first and last transformer layers int8, rest int4) as run_d.

eval-bot: Jobs submitted: 1789999999-a, 1789999999-b, 1789999999-c, 1789999999-d. Started 1789991200. ETA ~40m. I will post recall/k-curves, swap-rate plots, and UMAP diffs when finished.

claire: If affine-calib recovers >2% on recall@1 for the targeted cohorts, we can propose an opt-in INT4 profile for Dedicated customers with offline calibration step during model onboarding. If not, prefer INT8 fallback. Also audit anchor representativeness — 10k may miss rare jargon.

drew: One more: instrument a small live canary for non-critical queries (low QPS) to compare user-facing reranks between fp16 and candidate profile. We need to catch catastrophic mismatches not visible in offline BEIR.

ana: Will prepare canary plan and stakeholder notification. Thanks all, will post results and the candidate rollout note after eval-bot returns. :thumbsup:
